recognize_zh: 骨髓切片抗酸染色（Ziehl-Neelsen）在藍色背景下可見大量洋紅色細長桿菌，散在於間質並聚集在組織球內，在 HIV 病人強烈提示非結核分枝桿菌（Mycobacterium avium complex）感染。
features: Numerous slender, beaded magenta (acid-fast) bacilli scattered throughout the marrow stroma
Clusters of bacilli packed within histiocyte cytoplasm, forming dense red aggregates
Methylene blue counterstained cellular marrow with spindled histiocytes and mixed hematopoietic cells
Adjacent fat spaces; no well-formed caseating granuloma is evident in this field
A megakaryocyte-like large cell is visible at the lower edge
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy stained with Ziehl-Neelsen shows a cellular marrow infiltrated by sheets of histiocytes. Innumerable slender, beaded acid-fast bacilli are present, both free in the interstitium and packed within histiocyte cytoplasm. Well-formed granulomas are not evident in this field, in keeping with a poor granulomatous response in advanced immunosuppression. In an HIV-positive patient with a very low CD4 count, findings are consistent with disseminated Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex infection; culture or PCR is required for speciation.

ddx.vs: M. tuberculosis usually shows well-formed, often caseating granulomas with few bacilli, whereas MAC in AIDS shows sheets of foamy histiocytes with enormous bacillary loads; speciation requires culture or PCR.
Lepra bacilli form globi and are Fite-positive but weakly acid-fast with standard ZN, and marrow involvement in this clinical setting is exceptional.
Nocardia forms branching filaments that are only partially acid-fast on modified stains, unlike the short straight non-branching MAC rods.
